content:
We need retrosynthesis route up to 3 steps, leaves commercially available, total price <=9999. Need propose route using templates. We have some template for sulfonamide formation via reaction of aryl sulfonyl chloride with aniline. Template 733: Cl-S(=O)(=O)-Ar + NH2-Ar' -> Ar-SO2-NH-Ar'. That's good for forming sulfonamide bond.

Our target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Structure: two aromatic rings: a tolyl (para methyl phenyl) attached to sulfonamide nitrogen, sulfonyl attached to second phenyl which has a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (para-aminophenyl). So overall three fragments: tolyl amine (p-methyl aniline) as sulfonamide N; sulfonyl chloride derived from second phenyl sulfonyl chloride; and the second phenyl attached to an α,β-unsaturated amide with an aniline.

We can break retrosynthesis: disconnection 1: sulfonamide formation between p-toluidine (4-methylaniline) and 4-(trans-... )-phenylsulfonyl chloride. So step1: sulfonyl chloride + aniline.

Thus need sulfonyl chloride precursor: 4-(trans-... )-phenylsulfonyl chloride. That can be made from corresponding phenyl sulfonic acid or from chlorosulfonation of the phenyl ring. But maybe easier: start from 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride? However we need the phenyl bearing the side chain (C= C /C(=O)N-Ph-NH2). That side chain is an α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline. Could be formed via Heck coupling of an aryl bromide with acrylamide? Or via condensation of cinnamic acid derivative with aniline.

Simplify: we can form the α,β-unsaturated amide via amide coupling of trans-cinnamic acid (or trans-3-phenylacrylic acid) with aniline. Actually target side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N (an aniline attached to amide). That's trans-3-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide? Wait: The fragment is phenyl (c3ccccc3) attached to N (aniline) which is attached to carbonyl of the α,β-unsaturated chain. So it's an anilide of trans-cinnamic acid where the amide nitrogen is attached to an aniline (para-aminophenyl). So we need trans-cinnamic acid (or its derivative) and 4-aminophenylamine? Actually the amide is -C(=O)N-Ph-NH2 (anilide). So we need 4-aminophenylamine? No, the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3) which has an NH2 substituent (para?). The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N indicates an aniline with two nitrogens? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline with an NH at position 1 and another NH at position? That's a diamino benzene (para-diaminobenzene). Wait: c3ccccc3 is phenyl, preceded by N (attached to carbonyl) and followed by N (attached to phenyl). So it's an anilide where the amide nitrogen is attached to a phenyl that also has an NH2 substituent (para?). The SMILES "Nc3ccccc3N" indicates an aniline with an NH at position 1 (attached to carbonyl) and an NH2 at position? Actually the first N is attached to carbonyl, then aromatic ring, then N at the end attached to ring (as substituent). So it's 4-aminophenyl amide? The ring has two nitrogens: one attached to carbonyl (as amide) and one as free amine (para). So it's 4-aminophenyl amide.

Thus we need 4-aminophenylamine? Actually we need 4-aminophenylamine (p-phenylenediamine) as the aromatic amine that will be acylated with trans-cinnamic acid to give the amide, leaving the other amine free (the one attached to carbonyl). Wait orientation: The amide nitrogen is attached to the phenyl, so the phenyl's nitrogen is the amide N. The other N is free amine on the phenyl. So we need p-phenylenediamine (1,4-diaminobenzene). Then we need trans-cinnamic acid (or its activated derivative) to acylate one amine, leaving the other free.

Thus retrosynthesis steps:

Step A (final): sulfonamide formation between p-toluidine (4-methylaniline) and sulfonyl chloride derived from 4-(trans-cinnamoyl-anilide) phenyl sulfonyl chloride.

Step B: preparation of sulfonyl chloride from corresponding sulfonic acid or from chlorosulfonation of the phenyl bearing the side chain. Could use chlorosulfonation of the phenyl (with side chain already attached) to give sulfonyl chloride. So we need the phenyl with side chain (the aryl sulfonic acid precursor). That could be obtained via electrophilic aromatic substitution (chlorosulfonation) of the phenyl with side chain already present. So we need the aryl compound: 4-(trans-cinnamoyl-anilide) phenyl (no sulfonyl). That's the same as the second phenyl ring with side chain.

Thus Step B: chlorosulfonation of that aryl compound to give sulfonyl chloride.

Step C: synthesis of that aryl compound via amide coupling of trans-cinnamic acid (or its activated form) with p-phenylenediamine, then maybe protect the free amine? But we need free amine on para position after coupling; the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl, leaving the other amine free. That's fine.

Thus Step C: acylation of p-phenylenediamine with trans-cinnamic acid (or its activated acid chloride) to give the desired aryl amide.

We need commercially available precursors: p-toluidine (4-methylaniline) is cheap. p-phenylenediamine is cheap. trans-cinnamic acid is cheap. Chlorosulfonic acid reagent maybe not a purchasable "chemical" but we could use chlorosulfonic acid (ClSO3H) as reagent, but not a leaf. Leaves must be commercially available chemicals; reagents can be considered but maybe okay. However we need leaves as starting materials; reagents like chlorosulfonic acid are also purchasable.

Thus total steps: 3 steps (amide formation, chlorosulfonation, sulfonamide formation). All leaves: p-toluidine, p-phenylenediamine, trans-cinnamic acid, chlorosulfonic acid (or SO3Cl2). Prices: need to check.

Search for p-toluidine.
